ratings_why.fun: Two clear growth paths (clock or brood) that the capstones join, and fights full of strikes and hatchings; the board itself stays thin until the Herald at Tier 5.
ratings_why.distinct: Earns 8 over 7 because one fight clock is shared and both sides' attacks move it, and eggs go into enemy units, so the next opponent's visible board becomes a puzzle about which of their units will live three attacks. No current tribe plays like that.

verdict_why: Rules now read and the loops are bounded; what's left is numbers and one mid-game shape idea, which the owner can tune.

points.text: Tiers 3-4 have no unit that permanently buffs the board, so a clock comp can fall behind tall boards around turns 7-10. One Tier 4 card that gives Clockworks a small permanent buff each Chime, once a fight, would smooth the curve before the Herald.

Herald of Spring beside Bellows is the tribe's only real permanent line, so it will always be the target late. A second, weaker permanent path (say the Painter's Brood also feeding a Migrant-style body) would give Spike a choice.
Hawk-Barred Hen says 'the enemy across Dozes' but Lay falls back to a random enemy when that slot is empty. Say whether the random host also Dozes.
Winding Apprentice is a good early body and a late Ottilie engine piece, which is the right shape for a Tier 1 seed. Keep it.

standouts.why: Grand Horologe Ottilie Gugger turns every Start of Combat card into a Chime card, so early Hens and Apprentices stay useful to the end.
Little Gernegroß is a readable Tier 3 high roll: hide, wait three attacks, hatch at triple size.
Bellows-Hall Tuner makes positioning matter every turn and gives the clock build its own multiplier.

weakest.why: Weight-Hanger is a 1/5 that only speeds one strike; little reason to keep it past Tier 3.
Old Unruh is a 0/9 that does nothing alone; his value is all in what he speeds up, and he speeds the enemy's clock too.
Pattern-Book Painter grows only Chicks, which leave each fight, so the board gains nothing lasting from him.

flags.note: Herald between two golden Bellows triggers five times: +10/+10 permanent to every Clockwork each fight (+20/+20 golden Herald), and it sits safe in the back row before the first strike.
Red-Mouth with Ottilie, three Apprentices and four Hens strikes after nearly every attack and makes about 12 Heaves a strike; in-fight only, but it may end fights in a few strikes.
Hawk-Barred Hen with Ottilie keeps the enemy across asleep all fight; counterplay is killing a 3/3 or not putting the key unit across from it.
